monthly_review.summary: Pace and intensity increased significantly this month, but volume dropped sharply — suggesting a shift toward higher-quality, shorter efforts at the expense of aerobic base development.
monthly_review.highlight: This month’s average HR rose by +9 bpm while aerobic TE fell by 0.5 — indicating reduced efficiency at higher intensities, likely due to insufficient recovery or underdeveloped Zone 3–4 stamina.

goal_tracker.message: You need 33.4 more km across 6 sessions in the remaining 25 days — averaging 5.6 km per session — to match last month’s volume. Given your recent 10.0 km long run, this is achievable with three 6 km runs and three 5 km runs.

insights.title: Efficiency declined despite faster pace
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency dropped from 13.42 to 13.31 m/sec per bpm while avg pace improved — meaning you’re expending more HR effort for less speed gain, especially evident in the 10.0 km run (stride length dropped to 72.5 cm vs. 81.96 cm on 2.1 km), suggesting fatigue or form breakdown at distance.

insights.title: Zone 3–4 dominance without Zone 1–2 recovery balance
insights.body: This month’s HR zone distribution shows Z3+Z4 = 44% (vs. 22% last month), while Z1 collapsed from 36% to 13% — indicating insufficient low-intensity recovery work, which may explain the +9 bpm avg HR and reduced aerobic TE.

insights.title: Cadence increased but stride length decreased under load
insights.body: Cadence rose from 146 to 149 spm, yet stride length dropped from 81.96 cm (2.1 km) to 72.48 cm (10.0 km) — a 11.6% reduction — suggesting compensatory shortening under fatigue, likely contributing to higher vertical oscillation (9.2 cm on 7:03/km effort vs. 7.6–7.9 cm elsewhere).

insights.title: High-intensity density on same day
insights.body: On 2026-06-04, you completed three runs totaling 2.5 km — including a 7:03/km effort at 159 bpm (Zone 4) followed by two slower efforts — resulting in cumulative aerobic TE of 5.1 that day, exceeding last month’s highest single-day TE (3.5), with no recorded recovery metrics (e.g., HRV or sleep) to confirm readiness.

recommendations.action: Do your next run as a strict 5 km Zone 2 effort (HR ≤135 bpm, pace ~8:50–9:20/km) with cadence consciously held at 146–148 spm.
recommendations.reason: To rebuild Zone 2 aerobic foundation — currently only 13% of this month’s time — and lower avg HR back toward last month’s 136 bpm, supporting efficiency and recovery.

recommendations.action: Replace one upcoming run with a 20-min walk or mobility session focused on hip flexor and calf release, followed by 5 min of diaphragmatic breathing.
recommendations.reason: Your 2026-06-04 triple-run day showed elevated HR (159 bpm) and vertical oscillation (9.2 cm), signaling accumulated neuromuscular fatigue — active recovery will support ground contact time (currently 310–330 ms) and stride consistency.

recommendations.action: On your next 6–8 km run, break it into 3 × 2 km segments with 90 sec walk breaks; monitor cadence and aim to hold stride length ≥78 cm in each segment using stride length feedback.
recommendations.reason: To reinforce neuromuscular coordination under fatigue — your 10.0 km run showed 11.6% stride length drop — and prevent vertical oscillation creep above 8.5 cm.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish physiological and perceptual ease in Zone 2 while reinforcing efficient movement patterns under mild fatigue.
suggested_sessions: 3 × 2 km progressive run with walk breaks
